text:
james_cust: Hey support — we've got a persistent issue today. Our client sets region=query param (region=eu-west-1) and also sets X-Client-Region: eu-west-1 header, but requests keep landing in us-east-1. Latency spikes (~600-800ms) and some 401s. Started ~08:10 UTC. Any quick ideas?

sara_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK) and any routing headers you see in responses? Also what's the SDK version?

james_cust: SDK v1.4.0. Here's a curl we used from our EU infra:

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=eu-west-1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-35b","input":"hello"}'
```

james_cust: Response headers we logged (trimmed):
```
x-redwood-route: us-east-1
x-redwood-fallback: true
x-request-attempt: 2
content-length: 12
```

ben_infra: Interesting — fallback=true + attempt=2 suggests gateway tried eu-west, then fell back to us-east. Do you have the original response from the first attempt (attempt=1) or gateway logs?

marta_eng: Quick thought: older SDKs would send region both as query param and header; routing precedence changed recently. If the gateway sees conflicting signals it may choose a fallback path. But james said both show eu-west.

james_cust: We do have a longer raw trace (sanitized):
```
[08:10:12] incoming: region=query=eu-west-1; header=X-Client-Region=eu-west-1
[08:10:12] route_decision: prefer_region_header=false; preferred_region=eu-west-1
[08:10:12] attempt 1 -> target: eu-west-1.edge01 (connect timeout 250ms)
[08:10:13] attempt 2 -> target: us-east-1.edge05 (success)
[08:10:13] proxy_resp_headers: x-redwood-route=us-east-1; x-redwood-fallback=true
```

ryan_platform: That log line "prefer_region_header=false" is suspicious — routing policy should prefer header when present. I'll escalate to routing team.

sara_support: For a short-term workaround, can you force region via Authorization header region claim? Alternatively, remove query param so only header exists and test.

james_cust: Removing query param made it route correctly to eu-west in our staging test. So repro is: both present -> gateway sometimes picks fallback.

ben_infra: Thanks — that narrows it. Likely bug in the precedence evaluation when both param+header present and an edge endpoint times out. Gateway appears to mark original region unhealthy and then uses global fallback; but it should continue retrying EU nodes before failing over to US.

marta_eng: Can you run with TRACE routing logs enabled for a few minutes and paste output? Also include the SDK request id header x-rwd-req if present.
james_cust: Added trace logs, sent to this thread. The trace shows repeated oscillation on healthcheck questions, e.g.:
```
probe eu-west-1.edge01 -> 504
probe eu-west-1.edge02 -> 200
attempt pick: eu-west-1.edge02 (but DNS resolved incorrectly to us-east IP for some hosts in our VPC)
```

ryan_platform: Aha — there's a known DNS leak/misconfiguration in our VPC peering that can return cross-region IPs for some edge hostnames. If client network resolves eu-west hostnames to us-east IPs, healthchecks look flaky and gateway falls back. Eng routing should make region decision on the logical region tag not the resolved IP.

ben_infra: Assigning this to me + marta. Immediate mitigation for customers: 1) remove region query param 2) set X-Client-Region only 3) pin SDK to v1.4.1 (we'll release a patch that enforces header precedence).

james_cust: Ok we'll flip to header-only for now. Any ETA on the patch?

marta_eng: We reproduced in lab by forcing inconsistent DNS answers. Root cause: routing layer evaluated DNS-resolved IP health and then re-evaluated region preference incorrectly when health toggled. Patch will: prefer explicit region header over query param and treat DNS-resolved IP mismatches as region-internal transient errors (retry same region twice before global failover). Targeting a hotfix in the next 6 hours, rollback plan included.

sara_support: I'll send a customer-facing note with the workaround and ETA. james, can you confirm whether you want us to whitelist your org for the hotfix deploy sequence?

james_cust: Yes please. Appreciate the quick turnaround. Also curious about the billing/401s — saw intermittent 401s when routed to us-east due to token geofencing configured on our side. The header-only fix should avoid that.

ben_infra: Noted. We'll include your org in the first deploy wave. Also creating an internal postmortem ticket to add an observability signal: log which signal (header vs param vs path) produced the final region decision.

deploy-bot: [deploy] hotfix/routing-precedence -> staging (started) :rocket:

marta_eng: Patch merged to staging. Please retest once we push to prod. Patch includes additional routing debug logs (x-routing-decision).

james_cust: Verified staging — header-only requests now route to eu-west consistently. Thanks all.

sara_support: Closing loop: workaround = remove query param or upgrade to patched SDK when released. Eng will follow up with release notes and a short postmortem. :white_check_mark:
